name: Pack It Up!

pick.label: Pick a product
pick.heading: Pick something ordinary and give it a pack nobody needs
lead: Supermarkets are full of things wrapped in more packaging than they could ever need. Somewhere, someone designed every one of those boxes, and was probably very proud of it.
Choose something that usually comes with no packaging at all, or that can’t really be packed, and design the most over-the-top pack you can. *Make it feel expensive.*
pick.hint: Or click one to choose it.
pick.note: This is not a real packaging brief, it’s just for a bit of fun. Nobody is checking your costs or your recycling plan today. Next week, maybe.

rows: Something fancy, something funny, or something very simple.
Glass, cardboard, wood, tin, paper, something nobody has ever used before…
What shape is it, and how do you open it? Is opening it a little event?
Colours, typography, pictures, lots of text or almost none…
One short sentence that makes people pick it up off the shelf.

values.name: Knolle Reserve
values.material: A little wooden box full of straw, closed with a red wax seal.
values.shape: A perfect cube. You break the seal, lift the lid, and there it is, lying in the straw like the crown jewels.
values.look: Matt black, one line of gold text and a tiny drawing of a field in Brandenburg. No photo. If you need to see the potato, it’s not for you.
values.claim: Hand-picked in Brandenburg. One at a time. Slowly.

yours.label: Your pack
yours.heading: Your design
yours.lead: Fill it in on your own phone or laptop (it stays on your device), and be ready to tell the class about your pack in a few sentences.

rank.label: The ranking
rank.heading: Which pack wins?
rank.lead: Each student tells us about their pack in a few sentences. Add it, then argue it into place until everybody agrees.
